items.passage: For the mountain tops and moors, my boy, by a beautiful law of nature, compensate for their own poverty by yielding a wealth which the rich lowlands cannot yield. You do not understand? Then see. __Yon moor above can grow neither corn nor grass.__ But one thing it can grow, and does grow, without which we should have no corn nor grass, and that is--water. Not only does far more rain fall up there than falls here down below, but even in drought the high moors condense the moisture into dew, and so yield some water, even when the lowlands are burnt up with drought.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It disputes the speaker's earlier claim that the rich lowlands yield greater wealth than the moors.
It establishes the moor's apparent poverty before the speaker reveals its hidden value.
It explains why rain falls more heavily on high ground than on low ground.
It suggests that the boy should abandon farming on the moor above.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 황무지가 곡식도 풀도 기르지 못한다는 '빈곤'을 먼저 보여 준다. 이어지는 문장에서 화자는 그 황무지가 물이라는 귀한 것을 길러 낸다고 밝힌다. 따라서 B처럼 겉보기의 빈곤을 제시한 뒤 숨은 가치를 드러내는 기능을 한다. A는 저지대가 부유하다는 전제를 반박하지 않으므로 틀리고, C의 강우 이유는 밑줄 문장의 내용이 아니며, D의 농사 포기 권유는 지문에 없다.

items.passage: Certainly there is no nobler field for human effort than the insurance line of business--especially accident insurance. Ever since I have been a director in an accident-insurance company I have felt that I am a better man. Life has seemed more precious. Accidents have assumed a kindlier aspect. Distressing special providences have lost half their horror. I look upon a cripple now with affectionate interest--as an advertisement. I do not seem to care for poetry any more. I do not care for politics--even agriculture does not excite me.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward accident insurance?
options: Reluctant acceptance of a dull but necessary occupation
Exaggerated enthusiasm that reveals a comically narrow outlook
Quiet regret about having given up his former love of poetry and politics
Sincere sympathy for the people injured in accidents
items.explanation: 화자는 보험업을 '가장 고귀한 분야'라 부르며 지나치게 열광한다. 그러나 장애인을 '광고'로 본다거나 시와 정치에 더는 관심이 없다고 말하는 대목에서 그 열광이 우스꽝스럽게 편협함이 드러난다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 마지못한 수용, C의 후회, D의 진심 어린 동정은 모두 지문의 어조와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Intending to engrave the name later in the afternoon, I wrote it down in my order-book, and asked the lady for her address, so that I might send the chain to her the next day. But, no; she would not leave it. She must have the name engraved at once, right away, and must put the necklace herself on her little daughter. She would wait. Ah, how it all comes back to me! Well, I wished to obey the lady, and so set to work. But I saw immediately there was not space enough for the whole name. She was very sorry, poor lady, and then she said I should put on the two letters D. R. There they are, you see, my own work--you see that? And she paid me, and locked the chain on the baby's neck again--ah me! it is so strange!--and she went away.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the memory of the lady's visit?
options: Annoyance at the lady's impatient demands
Pride in having finished the engraving so quickly and skillfully
Wistful emotion at how vividly the moment returns
Doubt about whether the visit really happened
items.explanation: 화자는 '아, 모든 것이 되살아난다!'라고 외치며 그 기억에 감정적으로 반응한다. 또 '아 이런! 참 이상하다!'라는 탄식에서 아련하고 감상적인 태도가 드러난다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. 화자는 부인의 요구에 따르고자 했으므로 A의 짜증은 맞지 않고, 자신의 솜씨를 보여 주긴 하지만 B처럼 빠른 작업을 자랑하는 것은 아니며, D의 의심도 없다.

items.passage:
Was it last Autumn only, when I stood
At the field’s edge, and watched the red glow creep
Among the leaves, and saw the swift flame sweep
From spruce to hemlock, till the living wood
Became a devastated solitude?
For now, behold, old seeds, long years asleep,
Wake; and a legion of young birches leap
To life, and tell the ashes life is good.
O Love of long ago, when this mad fire
Is over, and the ruins of my soul
With the Spring wind the old quest would resume,--
When age knocks at the inn of youth’s desire,
Shall the new growth, now worthier of the goal,
Find still untenanted the chosen room?
items.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward the future of an old love?
options: Bitter certainty that the fire has destroyed the old love beyond any hope
Calm indifference toward the ruins left by the fire
Joyful confidence that youth can be fully restored
Hopeful uncertainty about whether that love will still welcome him
items.explanation: 화자는 불탄 숲에서 어린 자작나무가 다시 솟아나는 모습을 보며 생명이 좋다는 희망을 본다. 그러나 마지막에 새로 자란 자신이 그 '방'을 여전히 비어 있는 채로 찾을지 질문으로 끝맺어 불확실함을 드러낸다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 재생의 희망과 어긋나고, B의 무관심이나 C의 확신은 질문형 결말과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: One morning I put out some fresh meat upon the snow near my study window. Presently a crow came and carried it off, and alighted with it upon the ground in the vineyard. While he was eating of it, another crow came, and, alighting a few yards away, slowly walked up to within a few feet of this fellow and stopped. I expected to see a struggle over the food, as would have been the case with domestic fowls or animals. Nothing of the kind. The feeding crow stopped eating, regarded the other for a moment, made a gesture or two, and flew away. Then the second crow went up to the food, and proceeded to take his share.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the crows' behavior?
options: Surprised respect for their orderly sharing of the food
Mild disgust at their habit of stealing meat
Amused contempt for their awkward gestures
Fearful caution about the crows' boldness so close to his study window
items.explanation: 화자는 먹이를 두고 다툼이 벌어질 것이라 예상했지만 '전혀 그렇지 않았다'고 말한다. 먹던 까마귀가 몸짓을 하고 물러나 다른 까마귀가 몫을 차지하는 장면을 가축과 대조해 서술한다. 따라서 A처럼 예상 밖의 질서에 놀라며 존중하는 태도다. B의 혐오, C의 경멸, D의 두려움은 지문에 드러나지 않는다.

items.passage: I planted myself against the rock, and he started cautiously up the wall. Looking down the glare front of ice, it was not pleasant to consider at what velocity a slip would send me to the bottom, or at what angle, and to what probable depth, I should be projected into the ice-water. Indeed, the idea of such a sudden bath was so annoying that I lifted my eyes toward my companion. He reached my farthest point without great difficulty, and made a bold spring for the crack, reaching it without an inch to spare, and holding on wholly by his fingers.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward his position below the ice wall?
options: Calm confidence that a fall would cause no harm
Uneasy awareness of the danger a slip would bring
Open resentment toward his companion for the climb
Playful excitement about a sudden bath in ice-water
items.explanation: 화자는 미끄러지면 어떤 속도로 떨어질지 생각하는 것이 '유쾌하지 않았다'고 말한다. 또 얼음물에 빠질 생각이 너무 싫어 동료 쪽으로 눈을 들었다고 서술한다. 따라서 B처럼 위험을 불안하게 의식하는 태도다. A의 자신감, C의 원망, D의 장난스러운 흥분은 모두 지문과 어긋난다.

items.passage: On the contrary, there was the most abundant security and provision for Peggy Hedderwick in his presence there in her mother’s cottage, and his frankly undertaking to marry the lass at once, before competent witnesses. It was not from such a good end as this that her conscience and her minister alike had begun to frighten the widow. Her dear little Peggy would be a lady after all, and some day she would take her stand among the best and be freely acknowledged by the whole of the county side. She could not expect that just at first, but anyway she would be kept an honest and innocent woman. Her children, if she ever had children, would be born in lawful wedlock.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The widow fears that the hurried marriage will bring her daughter lasting shame and disgrace.
The minister persuades Peggy to refuse the proposal.
The widow comes to see the proposed marriage as a safe and hopeful future for Peggy.
Peggy plans to win acceptance from the whole county at once.
items.explanation: 지문은 그 남자가 증인 앞에서 바로 결혼하겠다고 나선 것이 페기에게 충분한 안전이 된다고 말한다. 과부는 딸이 결국 숙녀가 되고 정직한 여인으로 지켜질 것이라 기대한다. 따라서 C가 요지다. A는 과부의 두려움이 이런 좋은 결말에서 온 것이 아니라는 내용과 어긋나고, B의 거절 설득은 없으며, D는 처음부터 그런 기대를 할 수 없다는 내용과 반대다.

items.passage: Otto, then, had never penetrated into a character whose reserve was so like his own that he could not understand it. He loved his young wife, and kissed her; and he fancied, like so many men, that his consciousness of loving her was sufficient for all her wants. As for her position in the house, in the family, if it was uncomfortable, could he help that? Was not he himself weighed down by his difficulties, his responsibilities, the worry of universal deepening displeasure? What were the pinpricks she complained of compared to his wounds?
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To praise Otto for patiently enduring the many difficulties and responsibilities he faces
To describe the household duties that Otto's wife neglects
To show that Otto's wife openly complains to the whole family
To reveal how Otto's self-absorption keeps him from understanding his wife
items.explanation: 서술자는 오토가 아내의 성격을 꿰뚫어 본 적이 없으며 사랑한다는 자각만으로 충분하다고 착각한다고 말한다. 이어 자신의 상처에 비하면 아내의 불만은 바늘에 찔린 정도라고 여기는 오토의 생각을 보여 준다. 따라서 D처럼 자기중심성이 아내 이해를 막는다는 점을 드러내는 것이 목적이다. A의 칭찬, B의 집안일, C의 공개적 불평은 지문의 초점이 아니다.

items.passage:
The secret of thriving is thrift; saving of force; to get as much work as possible done with the least expenditure of power, the least jar and obstruction, the least wear and tear.

And the secret of thrift is knowledge. In proportion as you know the laws and nature of a subject, you will be able to work at it easily, surely, rapidly, successfully; instead of wasting your money or your energies in mistaken schemes, irregular efforts, which end in disappointment and exhaustion.

The secret of thrift, I say, is knowledge. The more you know, the more you can save yourself and that which belongs to you; and can do more work with less effort.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Knowledge allows people to work efficiently and avoid wasted effort.
Saving money matters far more than gaining knowledge about any particular subject.
Hard work without rest eventually leads to exhaustion.
Most schemes for thriving end in disappointment.
items.explanation: 글쓴이는 번영의 비결이 힘을 아끼는 절약이라고 한 뒤, 절약의 비결은 지식이라고 거듭 말한다. 많이 알수록 적은 노력으로 더 많은 일을 할 수 있다고 정리한다. 따라서 A가 요지다. B는 지식과 돈의 우선순위를 뒤집었고, C와 D는 잘못된 시도의 결과를 언급한 일부 내용을 과장한 것이다.

items.passage:
The emu meat became so tainted that it affected our bowels, and I had consequently to reserve it for the dog. As the nutritious qualities of our meat decreased, I had increased the daily allowance from five pounds to seven; allowing two pounds and a half for breakfast, the same quantity for luncheon, and two pounds for dinner. Mr. Roper had slowly recovered, but sufficiently to mount his horse without assistance.

We were sadly distressed for want of clothing. The few shirts which we had taken with us, became so worn and threadbare, that the slightest tension would tear them. To find materials for mending the body, we had to cut off the sleeves, and, when these were used, pieces were taken from the lower part of the shirt to mend the upper.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To explain how emu meat should be cooked on a journey
To describe the hardships the travelers faced as supplies wore out
To praise Mr. Roper for recovering without any help
To argue that future travelers should carry many more shirts and stronger clothing
items.explanation: 지문은 상한 에뮤 고기로 탈이 나 고기 배급을 늘려야 했던 사정을 전한다. 이어 셔츠가 해져 소매와 아랫자락을 잘라 기워야 했다고 서술한다. 따라서 B처럼 물자가 바닥나며 겪은 고난을 묘사하는 것이 목적이다. A의 조리법, C의 칭찬, D의 주장은 지문에 없다.

items.passage:
Somehow none of us were sorry to go. This was natural, so far as several were concerned, but rather curious as regarded those of the family who knew no drawback to the charms of the place. I suppose it was due to some instinctive consciousness of the influence which so many of the party had felt it impossible to resist or explain.

And the Rectory at Raxtrew was really a dear little place. It was so bright and open and sunny. Dormy's pale face was rosy with pleasure the first afternoon when he came rushing in to tell us that there were tame rabbits and a pair of guinea-pigs in an otherwise empty loose box in the stable-yard.

"Do come and look at them," he begged, and I went with him, pleased to see him so happy.
items.question: Based on the text, why does the narrator go with Dormy to the stable-yard?
options: She is glad to see him so happy and wishes to share his pleasure.
She wants to make sure the rabbits and guinea-pigs are safely locked in their box.
She hopes to escape an influence she felt in the Rectory.
She plans to choose one of the guinea-pigs for herself.
items.explanation: 도미는 집토끼와 기니피그를 발견하고 기쁨에 얼굴이 붉어져 와서 보러 가자고 조른다. 서술자는 그가 그렇게 행복한 것을 보고 기뻐하며 함께 간다고 직접 밝힌다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 안전 확인, D의 기니피그 선택은 지문에 없고, C의 영향력은 이전 장소에 관한 내용이며 새 사제관은 밝고 즐거운 곳으로 묘사된다.

items.passage: Surely the place was familiar to him? He knew that arched roof and these rough, stone walls. Why, it was here that he had been brought to die, and through that very door the false Rosamund had come to bid him farewell, who now returned to greet her in this same darksome den. Well, it was empty—doubtless she would soon come, and he waited, looking at the door. It did not stir; he heard no footsteps; nothing broke that utter silence. He turned again and stared about him. Something glinted on the ground yonder, towards the end of the vault, just where he had knelt before the executioner.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall mood of the text?
options: Festive and lighthearted
Eerie and suspenseful
Peaceful and drowsy
Bitter and accusing
items.explanation: 그는 자신이 죽으러 끌려왔던 어두운 지하실에서 문을 바라보며 기다린다. 발소리도 없고 '완전한 정적'만 흐르다가, 처형인 앞에 무릎 꿇었던 자리에서 무언가 반짝인다. 이런 서술은 B처럼 으스스하고 긴장감 있는 분위기를 만든다. A의 축제 분위기, C의 평온함, D의 원망은 지문과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: I thought there was something in the wind. Yes, I was sure of it, when you went out of the house to-day. I knew it by the looks of you, though I didn't say anything. Upon my word! And you call yourself a respectable man, and the father of a family! Going to a fair among all sorts of people,--at your time of life. Yes; and never think of taking your wife with you. Oh no! you can go and enjoy yourself out, with I don't know who: go out, and make yourself very pleasant, I dare say. Don't tell me; I hear what a nice companion Mr. Caudle is: what a good-tempered person. Ha! I only wish people could see you at home, that's all. But so it is with men.
items.question: Based on the text, what is the relationship between the speaker and Mr. Caudle?
options: She is a close friend who admires his cheerful company.
She is his employer scolding him for missing a day of work at the shop.
She is his wife who resents being left out of his outing.
She is a neighbor gossiping about his visits to fairs.
items.explanation: 화자는 그가 '가족의 아버지'라고 하면서 아내를 데려가지 않은 것을 탓한다. 또 사람들이 집에서의 그를 봐야 한다고 말하며 가정 안의 관계임을 드러낸다. 따라서 C처럼 소외된 데 분개하는 아내다. A의 감탄, B의 고용 관계, D의 이웃 험담은 모두 지문의 단서와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Just then there was the spark of a match against the darkness framed in by the window opposite. A hand and arm shone in the flicker of light across the upper sash. A tiny spark, tremulous at first, like a bird alighting on a frail branch, paused, steadied, and became fixed. In the light of a small taper the man caught a glimpse of a pale, long face in a frame of silver hair. It faded into the background. But above the candle he now saw, with arms outstretched as it seemed toward himself, a pink little angel with gauzy wings.

The man's heart gave a leap. Sudden memories thronged his brain, making him almost dizzy. At last they formulated into one smothered cry.
items.question: In the text, the pink little angel above the candle most likely symbolizes
options: the danger of a fire spreading through the window
the loneliness of the silver-haired figure in the window across the way
the man's fear of being watched by strangers
a sudden return of tender memories from the man's past
items.explanation: 촛불 위의 분홍 천사가 그를 향해 팔을 벌린 듯 보이자 그의 심장이 뛴다. 곧바로 '갑작스러운 기억들'이 몰려와 어지러울 정도라고 서술된다. 따라서 천사는 D처럼 과거의 다정한 기억이 되살아나는 것을 상징한다. A의 화재 위험, B의 외로움, C의 감시 공포는 지문의 반응과 연결되지 않는다.

items.passage:
By the beginning of summer Crescimir's place had all been restored and the house rebuilt on the summit of the knoll, far away from any danger of another flood.

It was a pretty cottage now, in the new, American style with a trellis-porch over which passion vines spread in the profusion of first growth. The flower garden and the long lines and square beds of the vegetable garden looked fresh and bright down by the arroyo.

The house had been completed by the middle of January and Crescimir by careful and steady work had brought back his fields to their former state. The Christchild still lived with him, always as merry as the day was long.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “as merry as the day was long” most nearly suggests that the Christchild was
options: busy working in the fields from morning to night
worried about the length of the summer days
cheerful and happy at all times
tired by the end of each long day
items.explanation: 이 구절은 하루가 긴 만큼 내내 즐거웠다는 비유적 표현이다. 집이 복구되고 정원이 밝고 산뜻하게 빛나는 문맥과 어울려 늘 명랑했다는 뜻이 된다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 '하루'라는 단어를 글자 그대로 시간이나 노동으로 해석했고, B의 걱정은 '명랑한'과 반대다.

items.passage:
The weight of the man had sunk him down deep into the soft cushion, so that there was nothing of him to be seen save the folds of the bell-shaped cloak, the red jewel, and the head. He looked like a coiled-up snake; the dark and glittering eyes also were those of a snake. Of his features, in the deep shade of the canopy and of the wide black turban, they could see nothing.

The aspect of this figure was so terrible and inhuman that the brethren trembled at the sight of him.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “looked like a coiled-up snake” most nearly suggests that the man appeared
options: tired and ready to fall asleep
small and easily overlooked
friendly despite his strange clothing
menacing and poised to strike
items.explanation: 남자가 쿠션 속에 몸을 깊이 묻은 모습을 똬리 튼 뱀에 비유하고, 눈 또한 뱀의 눈 같다고 한다. 이어 그 모습이 너무 무섭고 비인간적이어서 형제들이 떨었다고 서술한다. 따라서 D처럼 위협적이고 덮칠 듯한 인상이다. A의 피곤함, B의 왜소함, C의 친근함은 형제들의 두려움과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
I sat by the fire and watched it blaze,
And dreamed that she wrote me a letter,
And for that dream to the end of my days
To Fancy I owe myself debtor.

Next day there came the postman's knock,
The morning was bright and sunny,
And showed me a sheaf of circulars, stock
Attempts to get hold of my money.

'Mid correspondence of this dull kind
A dainty notelet lay hidden,
It seemed as though it had half a mind
To consider itself forbidden.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “had half a mind / To consider itself forbidden” most nearly suggests that the note
options: seemed shy, almost as if it should not be there
appeared official and demanded immediate payment
was too damaged by the mail to be read
looked identical to the dull circulars around it
items.explanation: 이 구절은 편지를 사람처럼 표현해 스스로 금지된 것이라 여길까 망설이는 듯하다고 말한다. 편지가 지루한 광고 우편물 사이에 '숨겨져' 있었다는 문맥과 함께 수줍게 숨은 인상을 준다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 돈을 노리는 광고물에 해당하고, C의 손상은 언급되지 않으며, D는 '앙증맞은' 편지와 광고물의 대조를 놓친다.

items.passage:
Progress there is in knowledge; and science has enabled the number of human beings capable of existing upon this earth to be indefinitely multiplied. But this is but a small triumph if the ratio of the good and bad, the wise and the foolish, the full and the hungry, remains unaffected. And we cheat ourselves with words when we conclude out of our material splendour an advance of the race.

In two things there is progress--progress in knowledge of the outward world, and progress in material wealth. This last, for the present, creates, perhaps, more evils than it relieves; but suppose this difficulty solved--suppose the wealth distributed, and every peasant living like a peer--what then?
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “we cheat ourselves with words” most nearly suggests that people
options: break the promises and agreements they have made with one another
deceive themselves by using flattering language about progress
lack the vocabulary to describe scientific discovery
argue too often about the meaning of words
items.explanation: 글쓴이는 과학이 인구를 늘린 것은 작은 승리일 뿐이며 선악과 현명함의 비율은 그대로라고 말한다. 그런데도 물질적 화려함에서 인류의 진보를 결론짓는 것을 '말로 스스로를 속인다'고 표현한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 약속 위반, C의 어휘 부족, D의 말다툼은 이 비유의 의미가 아니다.

items.passage:
During this period my mother had two sons, between whose ages there was a difference of about three years: the oldest was named Matthew, and the other Robert.

Health presided on every countenance, and vigor and strength characterized every exertion. Our mansion was a little paradise. The morning of my childish, happy days, will ever stand fresh in my remembrance, notwithstanding the many severe trials through which I have passed, in arriving at my present situation, at so advanced an age. Even at this remote period, the recollection of my pleasant home at my father's, of my parents, of my brothers and sister, and of the manner in which I was deprived of them all at once, affects me so powerfully, that I am almost overwhelmed with grief, that is seemingly insupportable.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “The morning of my childish, happy days” most nearly suggests
options: the early hours when the family began its daily work
a single morning the narrator remembers in detail
the early, joyful period of the narrator's life
a time of trial before the narrator reached old age
items.explanation: '아침'은 하루의 시작처럼 인생의 시작, 곧 어린 시절을 가리키는 비유다. 화자는 집을 '작은 낙원'이라 부르고 그 시절이 늘 생생하게 기억된다고 말한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 '아침'을 글자 그대로 받아들였고, D의 시련은 그 시절 이후에 온 것이다.

items.passage:
In addition to the usual attractions of such a resort, there was a circular pen with a pole planted in the centre of it to which was attached a certain two-thirds grown specimen of the common American black bear. “Tim” was a great pet and altogether ______. He found a comic side to every incident which came under his observation, and, seemingly, never had a serious thought or an unhappy moment.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: fierce
timid
sorrowful
comical
items.explanation: 빈칸 다음 문장에서 팀은 모든 일에서 우스운 면을 찾았고 심각한 생각이나 불행한 순간이 없었다고 한다. 또 큰 사랑을 받는 애완동물이었다는 점도 단서다. 따라서 D의 '익살스러운'이 가장 적절하다. A의 사나운, B의 겁 많은, C의 슬픈은 모두 이 단서와 반대된다.
